new_factory_hunk.placement: Append one named opt-in export plus its local fixed lifecycle types/constants; preserve existing getPool, adminQuery, adminExec, adminSession and closeAdminPool behavior. No package/DSN/pool configuration changes.
new_factory_hunk.api: adminRetiredSession<T>(run: (exec: { query<R extends QueryResultRow>(sql: string, params?: readonly unknown[]): Promise<R[]> }) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
new_factory_hunk.surface_limits: Same existing getPool().connect() client and configured principal. Query-only frozen callback port; no client/pool/socket access, owner name, arbitrary cleanup SQL hook, retry or release control exposed. Only E15 serial helper opts in; no generic owner mode. No operation-options API is necessary.
new_factory_hunk.always_retire: Exactly one client.release(true), on every opted-in outcome. Attach the exact client end/error and drain listeners before callback work. Installed pg-pool removes the checked-out client from its pool before invoking end; never invoke release() without destruction, DISCARD ALL or idle reuse on this branch. Observe end separately within the fixed bound; invocation of release(true) alone is not closure evidence.
new_factory_hunk.default_compatibility: Existing adminSession and all existing callers keep their current code/control flow and signatures. The known unverified-DISCARD/release hazard is NOT claimed fixed globally. No already-existing default caller is silently migrated. Only the new E15 owner operations use adminRetiredSession. A later default-wide hardening would require explicit separate scope; it is unnecessary to close the new consumer containment gap.

finite_lifecycle.action: Use existing pool connect (existing connectionTimeoutMillis 5000); before invoking callback, bind the exact returned client, immediate fixed error/end listeners, drain sequence and transaction-status capability. Require installed getTransactionStatus function and known idle I initial protocol status; unsupported capability or error => no callback/retire/closed failure. Do not inspect or retain connectionParameters credentials.

Start one fixed 20000ms callback/operation wall deadline after acquire. The callback is SQL-only atomic setup/read/restore, never the ordinary HTTP/RPC callback. Gate before query invocation: admission open, not invalidated/ended and no overlapping query. Only one query may be outstanding; concurrency rejects before driver work. Record and immediately observe the actual client.query promise independently of its returned row projection.

Install observation before invoking actual query. Each query completion requires both actual promise settlement and post-invocation drain/idle-ready protocol evidence; a rejected promise alone is insufficient. In a transaction, allow native I/T/E status for continued cleanup, but never invent rollback. Deliver original query failure only after its protocol drain; no raw error values are logged/persisted. Use the remaining wall deadline, not a new unbounded budget. No driver query_timeout or Promise.race result is accepted as backend completion.

Close admission synchronously when callback resolves/rejects or deadline/error fires. A normal successful result requires callback settled, no pending actual queries, post-query drain and getTransactionStatus()==I. A callback returning with pending work/open or failed transaction is misuse/unverified failure, not a later successful drain promotion. The helper must already have performed rollback/reset/identity and required catalog/ACL checks on this same client.

On every path, close admission before exactly-once release(true); observe the exact client end signal and bounded allSettled of all recorded query promises plus callback. Use one fixed 5000ms retirement/join deadline, no repeated release/end/query/retry. Clear all owned timers/listeners on success; on incomplete join retain the exact still-observed promises and closed custody facts until isolated job disposal. Late callback query attempts reject before any driver call. No new SQL can escape through the revoked query port.

Return callback value only if the successful pre-retirement conditions AND actual client end + all joins are established. Otherwise throw closed lifecycle failure preserving callback primary and cleanup uncertainty without raw text. If end or callback/query join is absent, report UNKNOWN custody; never claim server rollback or backend completion from a socket-close event. No future shared seam operation may proceed on that job after unverified state.

bounds.server_limits: The E15 helper sets transaction-local statement_timeout=5s, lock_timeout=1s, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=5s as part of each bounded operation before catalog mutation. These do not substitute for actual joins. No pool defaults, driver query_timeout, backend termination or extra cancellation connection are introduced.

driver_evidence.meaning: _handleErrorMessage calls handleError before ReadyForQuery. _handleReadyForQuery updates native transaction status, readyForQuery, completes active query and pulses queue. Thus a rejected query promise is not protocol settlement.

An empty drained queue emits drain; getTransactionStatus returns the most recent ReadyForQuery status. Read timeout calls the callback early; do not equate timeout or stale transaction status alone with query completion. Client end force-disconnects active/nonqueryable clients and awaits connection end.
release is exactly-once. A truthy destroy argument causes _remove; _remove removes the exact client from idle/client lists before end callback and never pushes it to idle reuse.
Socket close emits connection end; graceful end writes Terminate then closes the stream. Frontend closure is containment evidence, not independent historical/backend transaction outcome proof.

helper_interactions.scope: Only existing serial clock replacement/restoration, private clock reads, subject-before-authority barrier and projection fault replacement/restoration use the opt-in. Existing fixture principal and ordinary restricted JWT/HTTP/RPC clients remain unchanged. No row-isolated owner operation.
helper_interactions.atomic_operation: Each call has its own qualified same-client transaction. Before object mutation qualify actual session_user=current_user=postgres, existing owner SET authority, required schema grant authority, exact target OID/canonical-or-exact-owned-fault state/full shape/ACL. Publish bound replacement with only needed transient CREATE/SET LOCAL owner; reset to original executor, revoke/verify effective CREATE absence and stable metadata/ACL before COMMIT. The factory additionally requires final protocol I and retires the client.
helper_interactions.ordinary_callback: The successful publication operation must have returned (COMMIT/drain/client closure) before executing independent ordinary HTTP/RPC work; no DDL transaction is held around it. Factory callback captures no ordinary client. The helper retains all actual affected HTTP/body/request/query promises and releases gates before joining them.
helper_interactions.restoration: After success, assertion or SQL failure, wait for all affected actual ordinary work, then restore captured canonical definition plus full original OID/owner/ACL/non-body metadata in a separate qualified atomic adminRetiredSession. No restoration call races pending ordinary work. On known operation error cleanup rollback/reset/identity runs within the same admitted client before callback termination, with independent cleanup admission inside the remaining bound.
helper_interactions.uncertainty: Any uncertain COMMIT/rollback/reset/metadata/restore/admission timeout makes a module-local serial seam custody latch permanently invalid for that job. Reject subsequent shared seam mutation/private-clock assumptions before SQL; do not repeat COMMIT or restore on another connection to guess outcome. Destroyed local connection is not a verified restoration. Keep exact function OID/captured canonical state and finite phase/outcome custody internally; serialize only closed failure facts. Job operator owns disposal/resume, no automatic retry.
helper_interactions.scope_invariant: This lifecycle refinement does not weaken any C1/C2/C3/C5/C6/C7 obligation or add new callback/runtime authority. Restoring a changed committed definition still requires subsequent allocated native proof.

meaningful_control_plan: Execute actual new factory function from full source with explicit fake installed-compatible Pool/Client event ports; no copied lifecycle implementation or real DB. Assert exact same acquired client, one release(true), no release()/DISCARD/new pool/principal; every branch denies reuse.

Success: real query-promise port completion plus post-call drain/native status, same-session helper rollback/reset/identity/catalog proofs and client end are all required before return. Query rows/ordinary callback values preserve identity.

Early backend error and client-side query-timeout simulation: rejection before ReadyForQuery does not launch next cleanup query or return. Later drain permits known cleanup; absent drain causes bounded retirement/UNKNOWN.
Missing authority/unsafe OID/body/ACL and grant authority refuse before mutation; no unexpected SQL invocation. Private clock read executes only as exact owner with no EXEC grant.

Thrown assertion, SQL failure, COMMIT rejection, rollback/reset/identity/restore rejection and callback returning with pending query each preserve primary+cleanup outcomes, close late admission, retire once and prevent later shared seam assumptions.

Pending callback/query, missing/late client end, late attempted query after close and duplicate release hazards: all actual promises observed, timers disposed, no false settlement/reuse. UNKNOWN custody remains when bounded joins cannot establish completion.

Publication COMMIT and actual operation completion precede the independent ordinary request; callback never runs inside owner transaction. Finally releases gates and joins request/body/query work before canonical restoration; strict canonical OID/full metadata/ACL/effective public CREATE absence asserted.
